- Model consistently overestimates early in the 30-day horizon, especially in the first 5–7 days, then underestimates later — suggest adjusting initial forecast upward by 1–2% for short-term spikes.
- When sentiment is neutral (all 0.00), model exhibits strong mean-reversion bias toward lower prices, but true outcomes often show sharp upward moves after low points — correct by adding 2–5% to forecast if recent price dips are followed by sentiment-neutral or slightly positive signals.
- Overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., 49.61 → 50.08) are common — cap forecast at 10–15% above peak observed in prior 3–5 days.
- If true outcome shows sudden drop (e.g., 49.61 → 35.94), model often fails to adjust downward — apply downward correction of 5–10% if true outcome drops >10% from prior peak.
- Sentiment history is always zero — no behavioral signal — so do not adjust for sentiment unless later data shows non-zero sentiment (e.g., >0.30), then apply +3–5% to forecast if sentiment is positive.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts often misprice the 10–15th day (midpoint) — model tends to underestimate mid-range values — adjust midpoint forecast up by 2–4% if prior 10-day average is below 40.00.
- If true outcome shows a “rebound” after a low (e.g., 35.94 → 38.79), model often fails to capture — add 1–3% to forecast if prior 5-day average is below 35.00 and true outcome rises >1% from low.
